checks: If an interior point is missing from the finite closed recipient union, choose a ball inside the body and disjoint from the union. Each omitted trace and the exceptional uncovered set intersect the ball in null sets. Their finite union cannot contain a positive-volume ball.

The interior is dense in a full-dimensional convex body. For any boundary point, points on the segment from it toward a fixed interior ball are interior and approach that point. The recipient union is closed, so coverage includes every boundary point.

Intersect the pointwise cover with the supporting face and integrate the nonnegative measurable weight. Multiplication by the indicator can equivalently be read as restricting the integral, including weights with infinite values. Repeated traces are permitted, and in dimension one the supporting point has counting mass one.

A closed ambient inequality restricted to a fixed fiber is a closed halfspace when its continuous normal is nonzero and a constant true or false inequality otherwise. Mixed almost-everywhere coverage restricts to almost-everywhere coverage on each positive fiber because each nonnegative fiber contribution to the uncovered mass is zero.

overlap.comparison: Builds a specific finite closed critical-cap cover from compatible fibers and depth maxima. The present statement applies to an arbitrary finite almost-everywhere closed cover and derives local deletion and weighted face-trace domination.

Bounds the volumes in inclusion-minimal subcovers of exact closed covers. Its cap-volume inequalities do not give boundary coverage by the positive-volume members or the weighted supporting-face comparison.

Produces an oriented flux inequality from a common minimizing cap. It supplies the motivating exterior weight, while the present statement assumes a finite cover and transfers that weight to traces on the same face.

readability: Positive fiber is read as a fiber of positive continuous-dimensional Lebesgue measure, and the last sentence uses the summed-fiber mixed measure.

summary: The finite union of positive-volume closed caps covers the full body, and restricting this pointwise cover to the supporting face gives the weighted trace inequality on each positive fiber.
